title: Swap Even and Odd Bits
statement:
Treat a non-negative integer `N` as a 32-bit unsigned number. Number its bits from `0` (the least significant bit) to `31` (the most significant bit).

Swap **all even-position bits with the odd-position bits next to them**: for every `k` from `0` to `15`, exchange bit `2k` with bit `2k + 1`. Print the resulting integer.

For instance, `6` is `110` in binary, which has bit 1 and bit 2 set; after swapping the pairs (bit 0, bit 1) and (bit 2, bit 3) the set bits are bit 0 and bit 3, which is `9`.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer `N`.
outputFormat: Print the integer obtained after swapping the bits.

examples.explanation: 6 = 0110. The pair (bit 0, bit 1) is (0, 1) and becomes (1, 0); the pair (bit 2, bit 3) is (1, 0) and becomes (0, 1). The result is 1001 = 9.
85 = 01010101 has every even-position bit set. Swapping moves each one to the odd position beside it: 10101010 = 170.
All 32 bits are 1, so swapping adjacent bits changes nothing.

hints: Separate the bits at even positions from the bits at odd positions using two bit masks.
The mask for even positions in 32 bits is 0x55555555 and for odd positions is 0xAAAAAAAA.
Shift the even-position bits left by 1, shift the odd-position bits right by 1, and OR the two parts together.
